REL.note: Who may be called whose.  A possessive between two people (suus, or a genitive of a person) is only right for a relation the book has; without this the generator writes 'the mistress gives her woman honey'.  Each pair is symmetric — either side may claim it — and "*" stands for any person.  `roles` says what each of the book's cast counts as when it is the owner; a cast name is never the one owned ("his Julius" is no relation).  `one` lists the words nobody has two of: such a word is owned in the singular, and where both sides are words of that kind the relation is one to one, so the owner is singular too ('by her husbands' is refused, 'the sons … their father' is not).

SENSE.note: Judgements about a whole sentence rather than about one word, read by generate_sentences.py directly (build_vocab.py carries any block that is not a part of speech through untouched).  Each was a class the QA audit of 2026-09-11 found in a shipped bank.

wield.note: What one person holds in one hand.  A bare ablative singular of such a thing beside a plural subject is 'the horsemen fight with a sword' (QA M-8), so the pair is refused; the plural instrument, and the singular subject, are both left alone.

exit.note: Verbs whose prefix is 'out of'.  None of them may stand in a clause with in + accusative: 'colōnus in cubiculum exit' goes out into the bedroom (QA N-17).  ad + accusative is untouched — exīre ad forum is good Latin — and so is in + ablative.

carry.note: What nobody picks up and carries.  Without this the generator sends farmers 'to carry the asses' (QA N-17).  The verbs are the carrying verbs; the list is the animals and herds too big to be lifted, and it blocks them as object and as the subject of the passive alike.

passage.note: What may come and go through an opening, for a slot that declares `through: <the opening's slot>`.  A window keeps out the weather and a bird, not a flock, an ox or a person, so 'they shut the window so the flocks may not come' is refused (QA N-17).  An opening this table does not name lets anything through.

fear.note: Verbs of fearing.  Their English wants what is feared — 'that the enemies fear' stops halfway (QA N-18) — so one may not stand in a clause that names nothing in the accusative.  A clause that prints one (quem, eōs, nēminem, a slot in the accusative) is untouched.
